_patient.input_block:
63M, EW EMER. admission from EMERGENCY ROOM.
OUTCOME: discharged alive to SKILLED NURSING FACILITY
PRESENTING SYMPTOMS: Severe sepsis without septic shock; Adult failure to thrive
PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS: Sepsis due to Pseudomonas
ACTIVE DIAGNOSES: Sepsis due to Pseudomonas; Acute and chronic respiratory failure with hypercapnia; Acute and chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia; Pyothorax with fistula; Sjogren syndrome, unspecified; Chronic kidney disease, stage 4 (severe); Displacement of other specified internal prosthetic devices, implants and grafts, initial encounter; Urinary tract infection, site not specified; Bronchitis, not specified as acute or chronic; Pseudomonas (aeruginosa) (mallei) (pseudomallei) as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere; Klebsiella pneumoniae [K. pneumoniae] as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere; Anemia in other chronic diseases classified elsewhere
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Encounter for attention to tracheostomy; Personal history of tuberculosis; Personal history of nicotine dependence
PROCEDURES: Dilation of Left Main Bronchus with Intraluminal Device, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic; Dilation of Trachea with Intraluminal Device, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic; Drainage of Left Main Bronchus, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic; Drainage of Right Main Bronchus, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic; Dilation of Right Main Bronchus with Intraluminal Device, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic; Drainage of Trachea, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic, Diagnostic; Removal of Intraluminal Device from Tracheobronchial Tree, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic; Change Tracheostomy Device in Trachea, External Approach; Insertion of Infusion Device into Superior Vena Cava, Percutaneous Approach; Introduction of Nutritional Substance into Upper GI, Via Natural or Artificial Opening
MEDICATIONS: Sodium Chloride 0.9%  Flush 10mL IV; 0.9% Sodium Chloride (Mini Bag Plus) 100mL IV; CefePIME 2g IV; 0.9% Sodium Chloride 500mL IV; Potassium Chloride 40mEq IV; SW 200mL IV; Sodium Chloride 3% Inhalation Soln 5-10mL NEB; Heparin Flush (10 units/ml) 2mL IV; Calcium Gluconate 4g IV; Iso-Osmotic Dextrose 150mL IV; Vancomycin 750mg IV; Lactated Ringers 1000mL IV; Nystatin Oral Suspension 5mL PO; Atorvastatin 80mg PO/NG; Docusate Sodium 100mg PO/NG; Albumin 25% (12.5g / 50mL) 25g IV; Heparin 5000UNIT SC; Bag 2BAG IV; Magnesium Sulfate 4gm IV; Glucose Gel 15g PO; 5% Dextrose 200mL IV; Ciprofloxacin IV 400mg IV; Doxycycline Hyclate 100mg IV; Glucagon 1mg IM; Senna 8.6mg PO/NG; LORazepam 0.25mg IV; Azithromycin  500mg IV; Mirtazapine 15mg PO/NG; Insulin 0UNIT SC; Ondansetron 4mg IV; Potassium Chloride (Powder) 40mEq PO/NG; Fentanyl Citrate 75mcg IV; Iso-Osmotic Sodium Chloride 1BAG IV; Famotidine 20mg IV; Midazolam 2mg IV BOLUS; Lidocaine 1% (For PICC/Midline Insertions) 5mL SC; Dextrose 50% 12.5gm IV; Acetaminophen IV 1000mg IV; TraZODone 25mg PO/NG
MICROBIOLOGY: BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE: PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA [GENTAMICIN=S, TOBRAMYCIN=S, CEFTAZIDIME=S, CIPROFLOXACIN=S, PIPERACILLIN/TAZO=S, CEFEPIME=S, MEROPENEM=S] | BRONCHIAL WASHINGS: GRAM NEGATIVE ROD(S) | BRONCHIAL WASHINGS: YEAST
SERVICES: TSURG
WARDS: Trauma SICU (TSICU); Med/Surg; Emergency Department

[1] The patient presented with severe sepsis without septic shock and adult failure to thrive.
[2] The patient was diagnosed with sepsis due to Pseudomonas, acute and chronic respiratory failure with hypercapnia, acute and chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia, pyothorax with fistula, Sjogren syndrome, unspecified, chronic kidney disease, stage 4 (severe), displacement of other specified internal prosthetic devices, implants and grafts, initial encounter, urinary tract infection, site not specified, bronchitis, not specified as acute or chronic, Pseudomonas (aeruginosa) (mallei) (pseudomallei) as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere, Klebsiella pneumoniae [K. pneumoniae] as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere, and anemia in other chronic diseases classified elsewhere.
[3] The patient has a past medical history of attention to tracheostomy and personal history of tuberculosis and nicotine dependence.
[4] The patient underwent dilation of Left Main Bronchus with Intraluminal Device, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic; dilation of Trachea with Intraluminal Device, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic; drainage of Left Main Bronchus, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic; drainage of Right Main Bronchus, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic; dilation of Right Main Bronchus with Intraluminal Device, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic; drainage of Trachea, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic, Diagnostic; removal of Intraluminal Device from Tracheobronchial Tree, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic; change Tracheostomy Device in Trachea, External Approach; insertion of Infusion Device into Superior Vena Cava, Percutaneous Approach; and introduction of Nutritional Substance into Upper GI, Via Natural or Artificial Opening.
[5] The patient was treated with Sodium Chloride 0.9% Flush 10mL IV, 0.9% Sodium Chloride (Mini Bag Plus) 100mL IV, CefePIME 2g IV, 0.9% Sodium Chloride 500mL IV, Potassium Chloride 40mEq IV, SW 200mL IV, Sodium Chloride 3% Inhalation Soln 5-10mL NEB, Heparin Flush (10 units/ml) 2mL IV, Calcium Gluconate 4g IV, Iso-Osmotic Dextrose 150mL IV, Vancomycin 750mg IV, Lactated Ringers 1000mL IV, Nystatin Oral Suspension 5mL PO, Atorvastatin 80mg PO/NG, Docusate Sodium 100mg PO/NG, Albumin 25% (12.5g / 50mL) 25g IV, Heparin 5000UNIT SC, Bag 2BAG IV, Magnesium Sulfate 4gm IV, Glucose Gel 15g PO, 5% Dextrose 200mL IV, Ciprofloxacin IV 400mg IV, Doxycycline Hyclate 100mg IV, Glucagon 1mg IM, Senna 8.6mg PO/NG, LORazepam 0.25mg IV, Azithromycin 500mg IV, Mirtazapine 15mg PO/NG, Insulin 0UNIT SC, Ondansetron 4mg IV, Potassium Chloride (Powder) 40mEq PO/NG, Fentanyl Citrate 75mcg IV, Iso-Osmotic Sodium Chloride 1BAG IV, Famotidine 20mg IV, Midazolam 2mg IV BOLUS, Lidocaine 1% (For PICC/Midline Insertions) 5mL SC, Dextrose 50% 12.5gm IV, Acetaminophen IV 1000mg IV, and TraZODone 25mg PO/NG.
[6] The patient was admitted to the Trauma SICU (TSICU).
[7] The patient was discharged alive to a skilled nursing facility.
[8] Bronchoalveolar lavage grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which was sensitive to Gentamicin, Tobramycin, Ceftazidime, Ciprofloxacin, Piperacillin/Tazobactam, and Cefepime.
[9] Bronchial washings grew Gram Negative Rod(s).
[10] Bronchial washings grew Yeast.
